informal_statement: If a <= b and f is continuous on [a,b] with f(a) <= 0 <= f(b), then f has a zero in the closed interval [a,b]; endpoint zeros and a = b are allowed.
reason: Equivalent in the declared constructor/section context. At ScalarSuffixCertificate.lean:411-417, the source contract is `theorem oppositeFace_zero {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (ha : f a ≤ 0) (hb : 0 ≤ f b) : ∃ x ∈ Icc a b, f x = 0`. The IVT uses a <= b, continuity on [a,b], f(a) <= 0 and 0 <= f(b), and returns a zero in the closed interval. Equality at an endpoint and the degenerate case a=b are allowed; the author does not claim strict interior existence.
